source_text: Quod vero tu posuisti: Concupiscentiae malum est, quod vitat ubique conspectum et quaerit pudendo secretum [n229] ; ita et Manichaeus: Secretis - inquit - pudoribus agunt, quo tempore odio habent lucem, uti ne manifestentur opera eorum.
pass_a_gloss: But what you have placed: It is the evil of desire, which avoids sight everywhere and seeks a secret by being ashamed; so also the Manichaean: By secret shames, he says, they act, at which time they hold light in hatred, that their works not be manifested.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: As for your statement, ‘It is the evil of desire that everywhere avoids being seen and seeks privacy out of shame’ (Augustine, Marriage and Sexual Desire 1.8), Mani says the same: ‘They act in secret shame; at that time they hate the light, so that their deeds will not be exposed’ (John 3:20).

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Hating light lest deeds be exposed.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
